newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian panel for freer capital access for firms.
newsitem.headline: Indian panel for freer capital access for firms.

text.p: An official committee studying the capital convertibility of the Indian rupee on Tuesday said local firms should be allowed to access global capital markets to raise equity without prior approval of the government or central bank.
Floatation of Global Depositary Receipt (GDR) and ADR (American Depositary Receipts) are now subject to Reserve Bank of India (RBI) permission under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA).
The panel, in a report submitted to the RBI, also recommended easier access to external commercial borrowings.
External commercial borrowings (ECBs) are now permitted subject to an overall ceiling to Indian firms with restrictions on end use of these funds.
The panel recommended lifting the restrictions on end use.
It recommended that loans for periods with average maturity of 10 years and above to be kept outside the ceiling in the first phase (1997/98).
In the second phase (1998/99), loans with average maturity of seven years and above would be kept out of the ceiling.

The panel sought to allow Indian firms to issue foreign currency denominated bonds to residents, subject to rupee settlement and investment in foreign currency denominated bonds and deposits, subject again to rupee settlement.
The panel urging lifting the requirement of RBI approval on project exports by Indian firms.
It recommended that Indian exporters should be allowed to hold 100 percent of earnings in EEFC (exchange earning in foreign currency) accounts.
They could use these funds for permitted capital account transactions with cheque writing facility, it said.
